nodes.title: How to use
widgets_values:
# MiniMax H3 — 30 s UGC reel, one Run

One Run renders **two 15-second beats and joins them**: beat 1 starts from your
photo, beat 2 inherits the character from beat 1 automatically, and you get one
~30 s clip with one face, one wardrobe, one room and one voice.

## The one switch

**Second beat — 30 s total** is a boolean on the canvas.

- **on** (default) — both beats render, ~30 s out.
- **off** — only beat 1 renders, ~15 s out. The switches are lazy, so beat 2's
  checkpoint is never loaded and its sampling pass never runs. Use this while
  you are still iterating on beat 1; it costs about half the time.

## The four boxes

| Box | When | Sections it carries |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Cast & references** | set once | `subject_definitions` |
| **B · Beat 1** | per beat | `integrated_multimodal_description` |
| **C · Beat 2** | per beat | `summary`, `retention_analysis`, `detailed_description` |
| **D · Audio & music** | set once | `overall_soundscape`, `non_diegetic_music` |

Two `StringFormat` nodes join them, one per stage, because the two H3 modes take
different contracts. Beat 1 (FL2VA) gets a fixed instruction line + B + D. Beat 2
(Ref2VA) gets A + C + D, which lands the six sections in H3's mandated order:

    subject_definitions → summary → retention_analysis →
    detailed_description → overall_soundscape → non_diegetic_music

**Never delete the first line of a box** — that line is the section label.

Write **350–500 words** in the body of B (`integrated_multimodal_description`)
and of C (`detailed_description`). That range is the guide's figure for the body
field, not for the whole prompt, and an under-written body is the single most
common cause of identity drift. Each body carries three timecoded shots:
`[Shot 1]` with no timestamp, then `[Shot 2] At 00:05.000,` and
`[Shot 3] At 00:10.000,` — keep the comma.

Camera moves use **motion type + amplitude + speed** ("pushes in with small
amplitude at slow speed"). Leave medium amplitude and normal speed unstated.
Dialogue is `The woman with a warm, low voice (S1) says: <d>[English] ...</d>`,
and speaker ids are assigned in order of first vocal event, then reused.
`retention_analysis` never uses `(Sx)`.

## The seam is a hard cut

15 s is H3's ceiling **per generation** and no wiring changes that. Beat 2 is a
new pass that references beat 1, not a continuation of the same take, so the
join at 00:15 is a **hard cut**: same person, same room, same voice, but a new
camera setup. Write beat 2 as a deliberate cut — a new angle or a new position
in the room — and it reads as editing rather than as a glitch.

## References

Everything except <Picture 1> ships **bypassed**, and bypassed is safe: an
unwired reference socket is natively valid and the model simply does not use it.
Select the node and press Ctrl+B to un-bypass.

- `<Picture 1>` · **active** — your character. It is frame 0 of beat 1 and
  reference image 0 of beat 2, so it is the one photo that decides the face.
- `<Picture 2>` · product, `<Picture 3>` · location — optional.
- `<Video 2>` · style / motion reference — optional. It is *2* because
  `<Video 1>` is taken: that tag belongs to the automatic 3-second tail of beat 1
  that the graph feeds into beat 2. Tags follow connection order, and the titles
  here match what you type in the prompt.
- `<Audio 1>` · voice lock — optional, 5–10 s of clean speech.

H3's own limits, across all of them: **≤9 images · ≤3 videos (2–15 s each,
≤15 s total) · ≤3 audio · ≤12 files total.**

## Size and length

**megapixels 0.8** at 9:16 gives 672×1184 — the shipped default, and the one
that fits 15 s on a 24 GB card. **1.0** reaches H3's native cap of 768×1344 and
is visibly sharper, but 15 s at that size is the heaviest ask the model takes;
expect offloading, or drop to a single beat while you test it. On OOM go to
**0.4** before you shorten a beat.

**duration 15 s** feeds the frame-grid expression and lands on length 362, the
top of H3's trained 124–362 range. **steps 20**, sampler `res_multistep`,
scheduler `beta` — beta and normal outperform simple on reference-heavy
prompts, which both beats are by design. `ref_image_size` is **max** because UGC
lives on face and product-label fidelity; switch it to **match** for drafts.

## Outputs

`beat` — the joined clip. `lastframe` — its final frame as a PNG, written on
every Run. Feed that PNG into `<Picture 1>` if you want to hand-start a third
beat from where this one ended.

## Model links

[Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

**diffusion_models**

- [minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors) — beat 1
- [minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors) — beat 2

**text_encoders**

- [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors)

**vae**

- [minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors)
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)

## Model storage location

```
ComfyUI/
  models/
    diffusion_models/
      minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
      minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
    text_encoders/
      qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
    vae/
      minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors
      minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
```

Both subgraphs load the text encoder and both VAEs. ComfyUI caches loaded models
by filename, so the duplicate loader nodes cost nothing in VRAM and each stage
stays self-contained.

Every file above is downloaded by the launch script before ComfyUI starts. It
reads the URLs out of this graph, so a loader without a URL is a missing file.

nodes.title: A · Cast & references — set once
widgets_values:
subject_definitions: <Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1> — mid-twenties, warm olive skin with visible pores and a scatter of freckles across the nose, dark brown hair in a loose low bun with two strands left at the temples, bare skin apart from a sheer lip balm, wearing an oversized cream ribbed-knit sweater with the sleeves pushed to the forearm and a thin gold chain at the collarbone. She holds a 50 ml frosted-glass skincare bottle with a matte white pump and a small sans-serif label.

<Picture 1> is the authoritative reference for her face, hair, sweater and the bottle; everything else follows from it. If <Picture 2> is supplied it is a closer view of that same bottle and its label. If <Picture 3> is supplied it is the same apartment bathroom the scene plays in. If <Video 2> is supplied it sets camera style and motion only, never identity. Any reference that is not supplied is simply not used and nothing else in this description changes.

nodes.title: B · Beat 1 — first 15 s
widgets_values:
integrated_multimodal_description: Live-action, cinematic, filmed as one hand-held phone take in a small apartment bathroom, natural late-afternoon window light from camera left, shallow depth of field, visible skin texture and fine sensor grain, the faint unsteadiness of a real hand. The palette is cream, pale oak and brushed brass with one trailing green plant on the shelf.

[Shot 1] <Subject 1> stands at a white ceramic sink in the oversized cream ribbed-knit sweater, hair in the loose low bun with two strands at the temples. She looks straight into the lens, lifts the frosted-glass bottle beside her cheek and turns it slowly so the matte white pump catches the window light. Behind her a folded oatmeal towel hangs on a brass rail and the mirror shows the bathroom door standing ajar. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed and settles just past her shoulders. The woman with a warm, low voice (S1) says: <d>[English] Okay, three weeks in, and I finally have something honest to say about this one.</d>

[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, cut to a tight over-the-shoulder angle on her hands above the sink. She presses the pump once and a single pearl of cream lands on two fingertips, thick and faintly glossy under the window light. Water beads sit along the sink rim and the tap releases one slow drip. The camera tilts down with small amplitude at slow speed, following her hands, then holds. Her sleeve brushes the ceramic as she turns her wrist to show the texture. The woman (S1) says: <d>[English] One pump, damp skin, and it sinks in before I have finished counting to ten.</d>

[Shot 3] At 00:10.000, cut back to a straight-on medium shot framed in the mirror. She presses the cream across her cheekbones with flat fingers, blinks, and half-smiles at her own reflection as though catching herself doing it. The glass has not fogged; the light has dropped one shade warmer and the brass rail behind her has gone amber. The camera performs a static shot with no movement at all and lets her finish the thought. The woman (S1) says: <d>[English] That is it. No tingle, no film, no drama, just skin that behaves.</d> She caps the bottle, sets it down on the sink beside the tap with a light knock of glass on ceramic, and the frame holds a beat on her hand leaving the shot.

nodes.title: C · Beat 2 — second 15 s
widgets_values:
summary: [reference generation + audio reference] The second half of the same hand-held apartment-bathroom review. <Subject 1> from <Picture 1> keeps an identical face, hair, sweater and bottle, the room and window light continue from the tail of beat one, and the same warm low speaking voice carries through while she moves from the sink to the oak bench under the window to close the review.

retention_analysis: <Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - face, freckles, skin texture, the low bun with two loose temple strands, the thin gold chain and the cream ribbed-knit sweater are unchanged from <Picture 1>; framing and pose may change, the person may not.
<Picture 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the frosted-glass bottle, its matte white pump and the small sans-serif label read identically at every distance and angle.
<Video 1> (beat 1 tail): fully_preserved - the room, wall colour, brass rail, oatmeal towel, lens character, grain and the direction and warmth of the window light continue without a jump, and the room tone continues with them.
<Audio 1> (voice reference, when supplied): reference - timbre, pitch range and pacing of the speaking voice follow it.

detailed_description: Live-action, cinematic, the same hand-held phone take continuing in the same apartment bathroom, natural late-afternoon window light from camera left, shallow depth of field, visible skin texture and fine sensor grain. The palette stays cream, pale oak and brushed brass, and the trailing green plant is still on the shelf.

[Shot 1] <Subject 1> steps back from the sink and sits on the low oak bench beneath the window, the bottle still in her right hand. She rests her forearms on her knees, leans toward the lens and lifts the bottle into frame at chest height with the label turned out. The window rims her left cheek and the loose strands at her temple, and the sweater falls open at the sleeve. The camera trucks right with small amplitude at slow speed, following her down onto the bench, then holds. The woman with a warm, low voice (S1) says: <d>[English] So here is the part nobody puts in the caption.</d>

[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, cut to a close shot on the bottle standing on the windowsill beside a folded washcloth, her hand entering frame to turn the label square to the lens. Late light passes through the frosted glass and throws a soft band across the sill. Dust moves in the beam. The camera arc shots around the bottle with small amplitude at slow speed, keeping the label readable through the move, and her hand withdraws. She keeps talking off-frame, unhurried, one sentence at a time. The woman (S1) says: <d>[English] It took about two weeks before the dry patches along my jaw stopped coming back.</d>

[Shot 3] At 00:10.000, cut to a straight-on medium shot of her on the bench, the window blown out behind her shoulder. She shrugs once, looks down at her hands, then back into the lens and holds the look. Her cheeks catch a low sheen where the cream went on. The camera pulls out with small amplitude at slow speed until her hands and the bench edge are in frame, and stops. The woman (S1) says: <d>[English] That is the whole review. No transformation, no before and after, just one thing that finally does what it says.</d> She sets the bottle down on the bench beside her, the frame holds on her and the window, and the shot ends without a cut away.

nodes.title: D · Audio & music — set once
widgets_values:
overall_soundscape: Close, dry indoor acoustics of a small tiled bathroom, a short tight reverb tail on every consonant and no room hiss. One tap drip at irregular intervals, the click of the pump, fabric brushing along a sweater sleeve, the light knock of glass set down on ceramic. Traffic sits far outside a closed window, low and unintelligible. The speaking voice is close-miked at one to two feet from the phone, warm and low, unhurried, slightly breathy at the ends of sentences. No crowd, no overlapping speakers.

non_diegetic_music: Solo nylon-string guitar with a low upright bass, 82 BPM, 4/4, plucked eighth notes with the bass landing on beats one and three, no percussion. It enters four seconds in at low level, sits 12 dB under the voice, drops a further 4 dB under each spoken line and returns between them, and resolves on a held root note across the last two seconds.
